title: Beacon mod manifest
description: One JSON file per mod in mods/<id>.json. CI validates every manifest against this schema on every PR, then rebuilds the pinned commit from source and hashes the result -- nothing here is trusted at face value, it's just the pointer CI uses to go get and verify the real thing.

id.description: Unique, lowercase, matches the manifest filename (mods/<id>.json) and the mod's own PLUGIN_INFO id.

description.description: Localized short description, one entry per supported language. The store page and the in-app store are user-facing material, and this project requires Portuguese, English and Spanish for all user-facing text, so all three are required here. `name` stays a plain string on purpose: mod names are proper nouns ("Beacon Chest") and are not translated.

pinnedCommit.description: Full 40-char commit SHA. CI clones exactly this commit, never a branch or tag -- a moving ref would let the source change after review without anyone re-reviewing it.

entryProject.description: Path to the .csproj CI builds, relative to the repo root at repoUrl.

assemblyName.description: Expected output DLL file name, used to verify the build produced what this manifest claims it does.

injectable.description: Whether this mod requires the BepInEx bridge (see tbh-beacon-modkit). false means it's a pure Beacon-side plugin with no game-process injection at all.

sdkVersion.description: Minimum BeaconModKit SDK version this mod was built against, e.g. "1.0.0".

minBeaconVersion.description: Oldest Beacon version this mod is known to work on, as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Beacon compares it against its own version (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json) and blocks the install with a clear message instead of letting the mod fail at runtime. Optional: leave it out when the mod does not depend on anything version-specific.

requires.description: Ids of other mods that must be installed first. No shipped mod uses this today: every mod talks to Beacon directly over IPC and none depends on another (a deliberate decision, see the modkit's own specs). The field exists so a future mod that consumes data another mod exposes can declare it, instead of failing in a way the user cannot diagnose.
